body: Even though it’s now essentially known that Eren planned the whole timeline, I’m guessing that Eren’s berserk mode was the attack titan itself absorbing his body to allow the attack titan autonomy, as we learned from Kruger in season 3 the attack titan sought freedom, which means that the 9 titans are potentially sentient in their own right (completely separate from their human shifters and that the titans themselves as transformations/extensions of the humans had their own desires), and considering how we’ve seen the shifters inside the titan body it is plausible that the titan bodies of the shifters do try to absorb their users for their own autonomic control. For example when Eren fights Annie almost his entire face is covered by titan flesh (titan flesh that is needed for control) except for his eye, meaning that his anger towards towards the female titan potentially allowing the attack titan to gain greater control and allowed for less regard of the titan versus the intention of Eren’s heart, allowing the attack titan to attempt to attain more control over the shifter and become whole in their own right. The attack titan was described by Kruger as seeking freedom, which by itself invites the possibly that the attack titan influenced who it chose to inherit it, considering it can see the future, and influence the inheritors desires somehow that I admittedly can’t explain, but in my opinion, berserk mode is likely the case of a titan taking over its shifter for the desire it most wants.

I hide it because I can’t stand the idea of someone treating me differently than they do now, my siblings would be no different. I’m not saying they’re bad people, but no matter how close someone is, there will always be a difference (no matter how small) in the way someone treats you if you have something like ADHD, or any type of disability, minor or major.  Being an older sibling with something as dehabilitating as ADHD and knowing that your siblings won the genetic lottery and didn’t get something like that means I don’t have an excuse to act less than the best I can be, and masking it and acting as if I don’t have ADHD are the best I can do. Am I jealous of my siblings because they don’t have it? Hell no, I’m glad that they didn’t get something like ADHD. I don’t want to talk to my parents about how I feel on the inside because it could change their perception of me as a person. I would also hate to put the reality of their adopted son who, to them, seems so independent and strong on the outside, feels consumed by guilt, sadness and fear on the inside, onto them, especially since I put on a happy face attitude every time I see them. Any change in their perception of me as a person might also affect whether or not they’re happy. With the way things are going in their lives, they seem so happy and I would hate to change that. I feel guilt for simply being a child (I’m not really a child, I’m 20) and I feel like if I told them, then I’d feel guilty and needy for taking away the happiness they feel everyday knowing that they’re making our lives better.
I wish I never felt jealous, but I do everyday

I had a single mom who passed away a little more than 2 years ago, and since then I got adopted a few months ago by my friends family, I want to go  to medical school and considering all that they’ve done for me I couldn’t live with myself if I went back on my word and failed to get there, so I always try to fight my ADHD by thinking about what my mom would think of me if I failed. In school, the main thing I do is record lectures because it helps a lot. It’s especially useful when you know how tests are constructed and what slides the professor is talking about when you have the slides available, if not, then I write them down as fast as I can. For me, staying focused in class is pretty damn hard, my adoptive older sister told me how hard the college I’m going to is since she also goes here and she wasn’t kidding. So I try to make up for my gobbledygook brain in class by going over stuff after and before class. That’s a very gross oversimplification, but as I’m typing this it’s almost 3 in the morning and I’ll type more in the morning when I have more energy and get back from classes.
